title: Sharp charts with ideal contraction detect a dense trivial locus and injectivity
statement: Let $(X,M,\alpha)$ be a locally Noetherian fs log scheme [def-trf-fs-log-blowup, pqf-def-locnoeth], without assuming log regularity. At every geometric point $\bar x$ [def-weil-geometric-point], let $A=\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{X,\bar x}$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], and suppose that $A$ is a domain. Suppose also that there is an affine pointed etale neighbourhood $W\to X$ [def-weil-etale-morphism] with a chart $P\to M|_W$ identifying $P$ with $M_{\bar x}/A^\times$, where $P$ is finitely generated, integral and sharp (only $0$ is invertible), written additively. Write $a_W:P\to\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_W)$ for the chart and $a:P\to A$ for its germ. Assume that for every monoid ideal $J\subseteq P$ (a subset with $J+P\subseteq J$, including $\varnothing$), one has $a^{-1}((a(j):j\in J)A)=J$. Let $V\subseteq X$ be the locus of zero characteristic monoid. For any such chart and any finite generating list $p_1,\ldots,p_r$ of $P$, put $s_W=\prod_i a_W(p_i)$ and $s=\prod_i a(p_i)$, allowing $r=0$ and empty product $1$. Then $a(p)\neq0$ for every $p\in P$, $s\neq0$, $V\times_X W=D(s_W)$, and its pullback to $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is $D(s)$. The locus $V$ is open dense in $X$. The chart identifies $M_{\bar x}=P\oplus A^\times$, and the structural map $(p,u)\mapsto u a(p)$ on this stalk is injective. Every section of $M$ restricts to a unit on $V$. Here $D(t)$ denotes the open set of prime ideals not containing $t$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-finite-chart-triviality-locus] to obtain the open U, its exact triviality-locus equality, the two principal-open formulas for every finite chart list, and restriction of every log section to a unit on U.

Apply contraction to the empty monoid ideal. Its generated ring ideal is zero, so no chart monomial vanishes. In each domain strict henselization, every finite product of chart monomials is nonzero, including the empty product 1. This is the private Lean helper contracting_nonzero and Finset.prod_ne_zero_iff.

proof.text: Suppose $u a(p)=v a(q)$. Then $a(p)\in(a(q))A$, so contraction for the principal monoid ideal $q+P$ gives $p=q+r$ for some $r\in P$. Reversing the roles gives $q=p+t$ for $t\in P$. Cancellation in the integral monoid gives $r+t=0$; sharpness gives $r=t=0$, hence $p=q$. Cancelling the nonzero $a(p)$ in the domain gives $u=v$. This proves injectivity on the stated stalk.

proof.text: The sharp characteristic identification is not needed for the remaining product identification: ideal contraction and sharpness already made the structural product map injective. Apply the log-stalk structural map and the canonical ring comparison to equality of chart-with-unit images, using that unitsIn is the inverse on unit groups, to get equality of their structural products and hence of the pairs. The chart condition gives surjectivity after adjoining units in the geometric stalk ring; transport those units along the canonical ring isomorphism to obtain surjectivity for strict-henselization units. Combine this bijectivity and the structural injection with the nonvanishing, finite-product nonvanishing, density, and the geometric formulas.

For each geometric point, choose one of its contracting sharp charts and enumerate a finite generating set by Fin r. The product s is nonzero by empty-ideal contraction and the domain hypothesis. The geometric lemma gives the pullback formula for U. Construct the compatible evaluation homomorphism from the affine pointed-neighbourhood colimit A to the geometric field Omega, by taking the colimit of the prescribed marked evaluations. Its spectrum gives a lift l with l followed by the structural morphism rho equal to the given geometric point, as proved by the colimit coprojection formula. Let q=l(default); it lies above x. In the domain A the zero prime eta generalizes q. Therefore rho(eta) lies in every open neighbourhood of x, by continuity. Since s is nonzero, eta belongs to D(s), hence rho(eta) belongs to U. Choose a geometric point above each x in an arbitrary nonempty open by algebraically closing its residue field. The preceding construction gives a point of that open in U. Thus U is dense. Combine this with the algebra, stalk bijection, and geometric formulas and section restriction to obtain every conclusion.

It has no new nodes, and its statement and stmt_deps match live, where the item is still unsplit with no repair note. Sources: ILO Exp. VI 1.4 (PDF p.75) and VIII 3.4.1-3.4.3 (PDF p.116). The item is an agent-extracted criterion: contraction for all monoid ideals plus a domain strict henselization replace log regularity. proof_origin=agent is correct, and there is no cycle. Step 1: contraction with J=∅ gives a(p)≠0. The unit face is {0}, by sharpness and the isomorphism P≅M̄, so the chart pushout of def-trf-fs-log-blowup is P×A^×. Step 2: principal contraction, cancellativity and sharpness give p=q, and the domain A gives u=v. A non-sharp counterexample shows sharpness is needed. Step 3: characteristic zero holds iff the generator images are units. A unit in the strict-henselization colimit means nonzero residue; this follows from the cofiltered colimit in the cited limit definition, and I accept it as elementary. The pullback along π_W is D(s). Step 4: étale implies flat and lfp, which is open by the Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open (01UA), so V is a union of open images. Step 5: the kernel of A→Ω maps to x, (0) generalizes it, and s≠0, so ρ((0))∈V∩O; this gives density. Step 6: by the log axiom α^{-1}(O^×)≅O^×, units are étale-locally invertible and glue. proof_deps equals the union of step uses. The proof uses only definitions and Mathlib leaves, so no tool_uses are needed and there is no SGA citation. An rg -L search found no duplicate node. Edge cases checked: r=0, P=0, N→k[t] at 0, xy=0 (excluded by the domain hypothesis), non-sharp P=Z. No fixes.
